cases.question: How do I enable change data feed on a Delta table?
cases.answer:
Only changes made _after_ you enable the change data feed are recorded; past changes to a table are not captured. [1]

- Enabling column mapping on tables might break downstream operations that rely
  on Delta change data feed. [2]

In Delta Lake 2.1, tables with column mapping enabled support batch reads on change data feed as long as there are no non-additive schema changes. [3]

cases.question: How does VACUUM remove unused data files from a Delta table?
cases.answer:
The data files backing a Delta table are _never_ deleted automatically; data files are deleted only when you run [VACUUM](/delta-utility#remove-files-no-longer-referenced-by-a-delta-table). [1]

See
  [vacuum](/delta-utility/#remove-files-no-longer-referenced-by-a-delta-table)
  for details. [2]

You can remove files no longer referenced by a Delta table and are older than the retention threshold by running the `vacuum` command on the table. [3]

cases.question: What is schema enforcement for Delta tables?
cases.answer:
- Schema enforcement: Automatically handles schema variations to prevent insertion of bad records during ingestion. [1]

Delta Lake can automatically update the schema of a table as part of a DML transaction (either appending or overwriting), and make the schema compatible with the data being written. [2]

See [Idempotent table writes in foreachBatch](/delta-streaming/#idempotent-table-writes-in-foreachbatch) for details. [3]
